title: Critical turning points during the course of psychiatric diseases: a transdiagnostic approach
summary: Currently, the diagnosis of major psychiatric disorders is based on psychopathology and medical history according to DSM-5 criteria and may not be neurobiologically and therefore mechanistically valid. It is therefore not surprising that research to identify valid biomarkers for psychiatric disorders is steadily increasing. Currently, there are no objective biomarkers that allow differentiation between patients with psychiatric disorders, e.g. MDD, and those with schizophrenia or bipolar disorder. In this study, we would like to examine volatile organic compounds in exhaled breath for their suitability in supporting diagnosis and predicting therapy selection, and compare them with blood markers and those from the microbiome. Markers from exhaled air have the advantage of being non-invasive and very easy to collect, and we therefore expect them to offer advantages over more complex diagnostic procedures such as brain imaging or blood or cerebrospinal fluid diagnostics.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Diagnosis of a mental disorder
Written consent to participate in the study
The participant is able to understand the study procedures and information (capacity to consent)
Exclusion criteria:
Unable to give informed consent
Neurological disorders, except dementia
Diseases that impair brain function
Exclusion criterion for controls: Diagnosis of a psychiatric disorder according to DSM-V.
